messages:
maya: Quick follow-up to the onboarding RFC — I dug into the compatibility gaps from last week's runs. We need a short decision thread on minimum artifact manifest and smoke checks.
arjun: +1. can we limit to things we can run in CI (<= 8GB mem) for the initial gate?
li: If we do that we exclude a bunch of 30B+ models. Maybe two-tier: CI-smoke (fast) and staging-bench (longer) — both required for admission.
sophie: Agreed on two-tier. Proposal: CI-smoke = export validity + simple generation sanity + kernel ABI check. Staging-bench = perf sweep, KV cache correctness, and quantization roundtrip.
maya: That matches what I was thinking. For "export validity" we should require a trimmed manifest with: model_name, arch, hf_repo (if applicable), export_commit, config_hash, tokenizer_version, and a minimal sample prompt set.
arjun: We should add runtime-compatibility hints: expected max_seq, kv_cache_size, and preferred dtype (fp16,int8). Those help the runtime pick kernels automatically.
li: For the kernel/ABI check: bench-bot can run a tiny loop that loads weights and runs 2 steps with a deterministic seed, then compare hash of outputs. If mismatch -> fail.
ate: (typo) meant nate: bench-bot: I can add that. Would you be ok with output hash + layer-embedding checks (first/last layer) rather than full tensor compare to save bandwidth?
maya: Yes — hash + a few sentinel tensor checks. Also include a tolerance for float differences (abs < 1e-4 by default).
arjun: About quantization: do we require quantized artifacts to be provided or do we allow runtime to quantize on the fly?
sophie: For admission, require either explicit quantized artifacts or a validated quantization script + seed prompts to reproduce. We can't silently OOM on the serve path.
li: Another tradeoff: run-time kernel selection needs metadata from the model manifest about fused ops (e.g., flash_attn version). How strict do we make this? Mandatory or advisory?
maya: Make it advisory for now. If manifest says fused_ops:flash_v2 but runtime lacks it, staging-bench must run with fallback kernels and produce a perf delta report. If delta > 30% -> manual review.
arjun: Sounds reasonable. For gating thresholds: CI-smoke must pass 100% export + hash checks. Staging-bench must have QoR (quality) diffs under 1% BLEU/ROUGE on golden prompts and perf regression < 30% relative to baseline.
li: Golden prompts — where live? We need a small curated set per workload. I'll start a /eval/golden-prompts repo and add a per-model tag.
nate: Action item: bench-bot to implement three new checks: export_manifest lint, deterministic-output-hash, and perf-delta report. ETA: EOW for smoke checks, next sprint for perf sweep.
maya: Operational notes — make sure logs include model_id + manifest_commit in trace headers so Console can link admission results to rollouts.
sophie: Also add a user-visible reason code enum for failures (EXPORT_ERROR, ABI_MISMATCH, QNTZ_NO_REPRO, PERF_REGRESSION). That will help line-of-business debugging.
li: Edge cases: models with custom ops (XFormers-like) should be flagged during lint, require a vendor-provided operator bundle. We should allow a signed op package for private deployments.
arjun: Security: verify wheel/signature on any provided operator bundle. ops without signature -> blocked for hosted tier, allowed for private with opt-in.
maya: Final question: do we require a sample inference cost estimate in manifest (tokens/sec and mem)? Helpful but optional.
sophie: Optional for now, but strongly recommended. We'll surface recommended values in the manifest template.
bench-bot: scheduled smoke run queued for model "tbd-example/13B-test" by @maya. expected duration 90s.
nate: I'll follow up with a short doc describing the two-tier flow + manifest schema. Will share link here when done.
maya: Thanks — let's reconvene after the EOW smoke implementation. :thumbsup:
